2 of 6 types, DOWN from round 5's 3 of 6, and this is the finding that matters most. My calls, then the truth — A bishop/KING wrong, B king/BISHOP wrong, C bishop/QUEEN wrong, D queen/BISHOP wrong, E knight/KNIGHT, F rook/ROOK, G rook/ROOK, H knight/KNIGHT. 4 of 8 squares, 2 of 6 types.

READ THE ERROR PATTERN, because it is exactly what the metric now says and it is not the same failure as last round. I got BOTH rooks and BOTH knights, and I got them as PAIRS — F and G I called rooks off the same cue (concentric stepped courses and a notched block, a tower from above), E and H I called knights off the same cue (an elongated muzzle, an arched crescent neck). That is the ortho fix working: same-type men now look like each other, which is precisely what MAD 0.6585 measures. But all four of king, queen, bishop, bishop went into a single undifferentiated bucket and got scrambled among themselves — I called the king a bishop, the queen a bishop, and both bishops king and queen. Every one of those four reads as the same object: a pale robed figure with a domed helm, wide shoulders and a cape sweeping to one side, on a chamfered hexagonal plinth.

So the round bought CONSISTENCY, not IDENTIFIABILITY. Two rooks now agree that they are the same thing; a king and a bishop still agree that they are the same thing. The MAD test cannot separate those two properties, which is why 0.747 and 2-of-6 are not in contradiction — and it is why the metric passing is not the same as the round's stated point being met. The device collar's whole job was to break the K/Q/B tie by pocket count, and at the size these men occupy in a 1280x640 window I could not count a pocket on any of them.

critiqueDetail:
WHAT IS GENUINELY BETTER, and it is the thing the round was for. src/camera/ortho.ts is a correct, well-argued piece of work and it does exactly what round 5 asked for. The projection is a true parallel one — w row [0,0,0,1], not a long lens pretending — and it is installed on the world camera instance rather than by handing another piece a different camera object, with isOrthographicCamera swapped so the raycaster builds a parallel pick ray and the board's planar reflection stands down instead of solving an oblique clip that has no meaning here. The CEILING_Y reasoning is real engineering: a parallel projection has no eye point for the chamber's leaning piers to converge on, so the near plane is used as a section through the room at 7.0 m and the picket fence those piers would otherwise draw across White's back rank is simply cut off. The result is measurable and it is the number round 5 demanded: same-type 0.6585 against different-type 0.8815, from a raw crop on the square centre with no mirror correction and no re-centring. Round 5's ladder of corrected variants predicted 0.6266/0.8722 for the collar under a mirror fix; the real projection delivered 0.6585/0.8815. The diagnosis was right and the fix landed.

WHY THE ROUND STILL FAILS, IN ORDER OF SEVERITY.

FIRST, THE BOARD IS ONLY HALF UN-MIRRORED, AND THE HALF LEFT BEHIND IS THE HALF YOU TOUCH. Commit 8144ecc changed 20 lines of src/core/constants.ts and added tools/handcheck.mjs. That is the entire diff. Two other sites derive a file from a world x independently and neither was touched. The click hit test at src/game/interactive.ts:460 still reads `Math.round(hitPoint.x / SQUARE + 3.5)`; eleven lines further down the SAME function's column-pick fallback calls squareCentre() and gets the new convention, so boardSquare() now contradicts itself depending on whether your ray hit the plane or a piece. Measured, not inferred: I clicked the rendered a2 and the selection ring plus its two destination roundels appeared on h2, h3 and h4; rendered h2 selected a2; rendered g1 selected b1 and offered a3 and c3; rendered b1 selected g1 and offered f3 and h3; rendered e2 selected d2. That is a clean reflection about the centre file in every case. The shader at src/board/coords.ts:410 computes `gIdx = floor(w.x / uGlyphSq + 4.0)`, so the letter cut over the a-file — which now stands at x = +8.225 — is index 7, 'H'. The render agrees: the far kerb reads H G F E D C B A left to right, with 'A' at screen x 937 where h1 projects to 929 and 'H' at x 373 where a1 projects to 344. Round 5 listed 'the carved inscription reads H G F E D C B A' as one of its four proofs of the mirror. It still reads H G F E D C B A. That proof was never addressed; only the squares under it moved.

The reason this survived is worth naming, because it is a process failure and not a coding one: handcheck.mjs was written in the same commit as the fix, and it checks the one thing the fix changed. It projects four square centres and compares their x. It never issues a click and never reads a letter, so it reports 'CORRECT: a-file is LEFT of h-file' on a build where clicking the a-file moves the h-file piece. A harness authored alongside a fix tends to test the fix rather than the property.

SECOND, THE CAPTURE TOOL CANNOT PHOTOGRAPH THE THING THAT WAS BUILT. `wantsOrtho` is gated on `!world.capturing`, and capturing is set by the presence of ?shot and ?t, which tools/capture.mjs always sends. So the command in this round's own brief writes a file named play-ortho.png that is a perspective render, and measuring it gives 0.9273/0.9091 — still inverted, round 5's result. I only found the real number by driving the interactive page and taking a CDP screenshot. The gate is defensible in intent (the six film shots must not change) but it is written as 'never under capture' when what is meant is 'never for a film shot', and PLAY_SHOT is already excluded from SHOTS. As it stands the project has no reproducible artefact of its own play view, which is how a fixed camera regresses silently.

THIRD, THE METRIC IMPROVED AND THE HUMAN READING DID NOT. 0.747 is a real result and I am not discounting it, but it went with 2 of 6 types against round 5's 3 of 6, and the error pattern says why. MAD across a same-type pair measures whether two men LOOK ALIKE. It does not measure whether a man looks like WHAT HE IS. Under the parallel projection the first property is now excellent — I grouped both rooks and both knights correctly and confidently, from a shared cue, which I could not do at all last round. The second property is untouched: king, queen and both bishops are one pale robed figure with a domed helm and a swept cape, and I called all four of them wrong. Note what that does to the headline number — the three same-type pairs are rook, knight and bishop, and the bishop pair scores 0.4752 partly BECAUSE bishops are generic. A metric whose best score comes from the least distinctive piece is measuring similarity, not identity. The next round should not chase 0.747 downward; it should measure whether a K, Q and B crop can be told apart, which is a different test and one this build currently fails.

FOURTH, THE HIGHLIGHT COMPLAINT WAS NOT ADDRESSED AND HAS GOT WORSE: 48.906% blown at median 0.9176 against round 5's 39.80% at 0.851, peaking at 66.844% at 0.9582, with whole-frame fracBlown reaching 0.019777 against round 5's 0.0115. It now also demonstrably bleeds onto neighbours (a black pawn one square away read 13.047% blown) and the capture debris keeps an empty square 61.469% blown two moves later. The still frame remains clean — 0.00035 fracBlown, median 0.1098, entropy 6.141 on the live ortho frame, 0.00074 / 0.1216 / 6.586 on the capture — so this is entirely a live-play defect and entirely invisible to the capture pipeline, which is the same blind spot as the second finding.

ONE UNAMBIGUOUS NEXT MOVE. Delete the two stale conversions and prove it with a harness that clicks. Concretely: replace src/game/interactive.ts:460-461 with a call to squareAt() from constants.ts so there is exactly one inverse of squareCentre in the codebase, flip the glyph index at src/board/coords.ts:410 to `floor(-w.x / uGlyphSq + 4.0)`, and extend handcheck.mjs so it (a) clicks the projected centre of a1 and asserts the selection ring lands on a1, and (b) samples the kerb where the a-file letter is carved and asserts it is an A, not an H. Those two assertions are the ones that would have caught this, and neither of them is expensive.
